config.title: Build outbound webhook retry queue

intro.title: Build outbound webhook retry queue
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple outbound webhook retry queue using Node.js. You will learn how to handle failed webhook calls by storing them in a queue and retrying them later. The core programming concept is using an array as a basic in-memory queue to manage retry tasks. You will work with JavaScript functions, timers, and error handling to implement the retry logic. This project introduces you to fundamental queue operations and asynchronous task management in a backend context.
intro.usecase: Webhook retry queues are essential in production systems where reliable third-party integrations are critical. You'll see this pattern in payment processing platforms like Stripe, which must guarantee transaction notifications reach merchant systems, or in e-commerce platforms that sync inventory updates to external warehouse management systems. Developer dashboards for services like Twilio or SendGrid prominently display webhook delivery status and retry logs, allowing engineers to monitor integration health. When implementing notification systems, user activity feeds, or data synchronization between microservices, robust retry logic prevents data loss during temporary network failures or service outages.

objectives: Construct a retry queue data structure using JavaScript arrays
Implement a function to add failed webhook requests to the retry queue
Configure a scheduled job to process queued retry attempts
Apply exponential backoff logic to calculate retry intervals
Manipulate queue items to track retry counts and timestamps
Initialize a Node.js application with queue management dependencies
Control queue processing to prevent duplicate retry attempts

steps.title: Implement exponential backoff delay
steps.instruction: Inside the WebhookRetryQueue class, create a method named calculateDelay that takes a retryCount parameter and returns a delay value using exponential backoff (base delay * 2^retryCount).
steps.hint: The method should multiply the retryDelay property by 2 raised to the power of retryCount. Use Math.pow(2, retryCount) for the exponent calculation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebhookRetryQueue class will have a calculateDelay method that implements exponential backoff for retry timing.
successCriteria: The calculateDelay method exists in the class, takes retryCount as a parameter, and returns this.retryDelay * Math.pow(2, retryCount).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the exponential backoff delay calculation. This will make retry attempts more intelligent by increasing delays between attempts.

steps.feedbackWrong: The calculateDelay method is missing or incorrect. Create a method that takes retryCount and returns this.retryDelay * Math.pow(2, retryCount).
